concept.name: Cross-validation
concept.definition: A resampling procedure that repeatedly fits a model on one subset and evaluates it on held-out observations to estimate generalization and compare choices.
concept.intuition: It estimates how a fitted choice behaves on observations that were not used to fit that choice.
concept.mechanics: Choose a splitter consistent with the data-generating process, fit the entire pipeline inside each training fold, score each held-out fold, and aggregate the scores.
concept.failure_modes: Random splitting, overlapping labels, repeated tuning, or an unprotected final test set can produce optimistic estimates.
concept.misconceptions: Validation measures conditional generalization under a split design; it does not guarantee future market performance.
concept.example: Five-fold cross-validation trains on four folds and scores the fifth five times, so every row is evaluated out of fold once.
